1. Executive Summary

122: 123:

124: The 2_DATA_ENCODER stage of the KNIRVHASHER pipeline stalls during 125: the NRV encoder phase because nrv_encoder.go contains only a 126: placeholder Run() method (lines 38–43). The Apache Flight stream 127: that should read .arrow batches from the miner_processed 128: KNIRVBASE collection was never implemented. Additionally, there is no readiness 129: contract between 1_DATA_MINER and 2_DATA_ENCODER, 130: so the encoder attempts to read from a collection that may not yet contain data. 131:

132: 133:

134: This plan specifies four targeted fixes: 135:

136:
    137:
  1. Flight stream client — replace the stub with full streaming logic
    2. 138:
  2. Readiness probes — poll the miner_processed collection before consuming
    3. 139:
  3. Exponential backoff/retry — prevent aggressive blocking on empty streams
    4. 140:
  4. Pipeline handshake — add atomic signals so the miner signals readiness
    5. 141:
142: 143:
144: Impact: Without these fixes the encoder silently returns nil 145: (the placeholder body at line 42), producing zero .nrv brackets. Downstream 146: 3_DATA_TRAINER receives empty input, causing the entire pipeline to 147: produce no trained seeds. 148:
149: 150: 151:

3. Problem Statement

236: 237:
238: When the 2_DATA_ENCODER pipeline stage runs, NRVEncoder.Run() 239: executes the placeholder body at nrv_encoder.go:41–42: 240:
241: 242: 
243: func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
244:     // TODO: Implement Flight stream reading from knirvbase
245:     // This is a placeholder implementation
246:     _ = memory.NewGoAllocator()
247:     return nil                                   // ← NEVER STREAMS DATA
248: }
249:
250: 251:

252: This produces zero .nrv brackets, resulting in an empty 253: encoder_output collection. The 3_DATA_TRAINER stage then processes nothing, 254: and the pipeline completes without any trained seeds. The user sees a “successful” 255: run with no actionable output. 256:

257: 258: 259:

4. Root Cause Analysis

260: 261:

4.1 Unimplemented Data Ingestion

262: 263:

Primary cause. The Run() method (lines 38–43) was 264: left as a TODO placeholder. The design document 265: (docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md:§3.2) specifies the intended 266: implementation:

267: 268: 
269: // DESIGN-INTENDED IMPLEMENTATION (from docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md:449-484)
270: func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
271:     stream, err := e.db.Collection("miner_processed").FlightStream(ctx)
272:     if err != nil {
273:         return fmt.Errorf("open miner_processed flight stream: %w", err)
274:     }
275:     for entry := range stream {
276:         arrowPath, _ := entry.Payload["arrow_path"].(string)
277:         records, err := loadArrowBatch(arrowPath)
278:         // ... encode each record via TensorPacker.Orchestrate ...
279:         // ... write bracket via NRVWriter.WriteBracket ...
280:     }
281:     return nil
282: }
283:
284: 285:

Key gaps:

286:
    287:
  • The knirvbase.Collection interface (defined in 288: packages/KNIRVBASE/pkg/knirvbase/knirvbase.go:124–133) 289: does not currently expose a FlightStream method. 290: It exposes Insert, Find, FindAll, 291: Update, Delete, AttachToNetwork, 292: DetachFromNetwork, and ForceSync. 293:
    • 294:
  • The Flight functionality lives in KNIRVBASE’s internal packages 295: (internal/network/flight_server.go), not in the public 296: Collection interface. 297:
    • 298:
  • loadArrowBatch does not exist yet. The current 299: arrow_writer.go writes file-based .arrow IPC (to disk), 300: but the encoder needs to mmap + read them back. 301:
    • 302:
303: 304:

4.2 Dependency Chain Breakage

305: 306:

307: The current 1_DATA_MINER/internal/app/miner_app.go’s 308: MinerApp.Run() is file-based (globs *.md from a local 309: directory, writes .arrow files to a local directory). It does not 310: write to the miner_processed KNIRVBASE collection; 311: there is no Flight stream between the miner and the encoder. 312:

313: 314:
315: Mismatch: The encoder assumes data arrives via KNIRVBASE Flight 316: (collections + streaming), but the miner writes flat files to disk. The two stages 317: have incompatible data transfer mechanisms. 318:
319: 320:

321: As a result, even if the Flight client were implemented in nrv_encoder.go, 322: it would open a stream to miner_processed and immediately receive a 323: closed/empty stream because no data was ever inserted into that 324: collection. 325:

326: 327:

4.3 Resource Contention

328: 329:

330: All pipeline stages share a single knirvbase.DB instance (per the architecture 331: decision in docs/KNIRVHASHER_Implementation.md line 28: “all 332: pipeline stages share the same db handle”). If 1_DATA_MINER and 333: 2_DATA_ENCODER ever run concurrently: 334:

335:
    336:
  • The miner may hold a lock on the miner_processed storage while writing 337: .arrow files
    • 338:
  • The encoder’s Flight stream initialization may attempt to read partially-written 339: data
    • 340:
  • No atomic signal exists to indicate “all .arrow files written and 341: registered”
    • 342:
343: 344:

While the current pipeline is sequential (one stage at a time), the design explicitly 345: allows parallel phases within a job. This contention becomes a real risk once parallelism 346: is enabled.

347: 348: 349:

381: // Run opens a Flight stream on the miner_processed collection, reads each
382: // .arrow file path from entry metadata, memory-maps the IPC file, and
383: // encodes every SecurityRecord row into a .nrv Bracket via NRVWriter.
384: func (e *NRVEncoder) Run(ctx context.Context) error {
385:     // 1. Open the collection in streaming mode
386:     //    (Fallback: if FlightStream is not available on Collection interface,
387:     //     use the underlying NRVStorage/Dataset directly.)
388:     coll := e.db.Collection("miner_processed")
389: 
390:     // 2. List all entries to discover .arrow file paths
391:     //    (The miner registers each .arrow file path as a doc in miner_processed
392:     //     with payload: {"arrow_path": "/path/to/doc.arrow"})
393:     entries, err := coll.FindAll(ctx)
394:     if err != nil {
395:         return fmt.Errorf("list miner_processed entries: %w", err)
396:     }
397:     if len(entries) == 0 {
398:         return fmt.Errorf("miner_processed collection is empty: no .arrow files found")
399:     }
400: 
401:     // 3. For each entry, locate and mmap the .arrow file
402:     for _, entry := range entries {
403:         if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
404:             return err
405:         }
406: 
407:         payload, ok := entry["payload"].(map[string]interface{})
408:         if !ok {
409:             log.Printf("nrv_encoder: entry %v has no payload, skipping", entry["id"])
410:             continue
411:         }
412:         arrowPath, ok := payload["arrow_path"].(string)
413:         if !ok || arrowPath == "" {
414:             log.Printf("nrv_encoder: entry %v has no arrow_path, skipping", entry["id"])
415:             continue
416:         }
417: 
418:         records, err := loadArrowBatch(arrowPath)
419:         if err != nil {
420:             log.Printf("nrv_encoder: load %s: %v", arrowPath, err)
421:             continue
422:         }
423: 
424:         // 4. Encode each SecurityRecord into a 12-slot bracket
425:         for i, rec := range records {
426:             slots := e.packer.Orchestrate(rec.ToSlotVector(), uint16(i), rec.DomainSig)
427:             bracket := &knirvbase.Bracket{
428:                 Projections:   internal.SlotsToProjections(slots[:4]),
429:                 SyntacticByte: uint8(slots[4] & 0xFF),
430:                 DepHead:       uint8(slots[5]),
431:                 IntentFlags:   uint8(slots[9]),
432:                 DomainSig:     uint16(slots[10]),
433:                 ContextMemory: internal.Slots6to8(slots[6:9]),
434:                 GoldenSeed:    slots[11],
435:             }
436:             if err := e.writer.WriteBracket(bracket); err != nil {
437:                 log.Printf("nrv_encoder: write bracket %d: %v", i, err)
438:             }
439:         }
440:     }
441: 
442:     log.Printf("nrv_encoder: completed, processed %d entries", len(entries))
443:     return nil
444: }

447: // and returns them. Uses os.Mmap for zero-copy where available.
448: func loadArrowBatch(path string) ([]*internal.SecurityRecord, error) {
449:     f, err := os.Open(path)
450:     if err != nil {
451:         return nil, fmt.Errorf("open arrow file: %w", err)
452:     }
453:     defer f.Close()
454: 
455:     reader, err := ipc.NewFileReader(f)
456:     if err != nil {
457:         return nil, fmt.Errorf("new arrow reader: %w", err)
458:     }
459:     defer reader.Close()
460: 
461:     schema := reader.Schema()
462:     colIndex := make(map[string]int)
463:     for i, field := range schema.Fields() {
464:         colIndex[field.Name] = i
465:     }
466: 
467:     var records []*internal.SecurityRecord
468: 
469:     for i := 0; i < int(reader.NumRecords()); i++ {
470:         rec, err := reader.Record(i)

472:             break
473:         }
474:         for row := 0; row < int(rec.NumRows()); row++ {
475:             sr := &internal.SecurityRecord{}
476:             if idx, ok := colIndex["file_name"]; ok {
477:                 if col := rec.Column(idx); col != nil {
478:                     if arr, ok := col.(*array.String); ok {
479:                         sr.FileName = arr.Value(row)

481:                 }
482:             }

494:                     }
495:                 }
496:             }

581: // defaultPollInterval is how often we check for collection readiness.
582: const defaultPollInterval = 500 * time.Millisecond
583: 
584: // defaultWaitTimeout is the maximum time we wait for the collection to be ready.
585: const defaultWaitTimeout = 5 * time.Minute
586: 
587: // WaitForCollectionReady polls the miner_processed collection until it contains
588: // entries or the context is cancelled. Returns the number of entries found.
589: func WaitForCollectionReady(ctx context.Context, coll knirvbase.Collection) (int, error) {
590:     deadline, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, defaultWaitTimeout)
591:     defer cancel()
592: 
593:     ticker := time.NewTicker(defaultPollInterval)
594:     defer ticker.Stop()
595: 
596:     for {
597:         select {
598:         case <-deadline.Done():
599:             return 0, fmt.Errorf("timeout waiting for miner_processed: %w", deadline.Err())
600:         case <-ticker.C:
601:             entries, err := coll.FindAll(ctx)
602:             if err != nil {
603:                 // Transient error — keep polling
604:                 log.Printf("readiness: transient error on FindAll: %v", err)
605:                 continue
606:             }
607:             if len(entries) > 0 {
608:                 log.Printf("readiness: miner_processed ready with %d entries", len(entries))
609:                 return len(entries), nil
610:             }
611:             log.Printf("readiness: miner_processed empty, retrying...")
612:         }
613:     }
614: }

Add a reusable retry helper, copied from the codebase’s established 639: APIClient pattern 640: (packages/KNIRVCHAIN/internal/resilience/api_client.go):

641: 642: 
643: // ── nrv_encoder.go (addition) ──
644: 
645: const (
646:     maxRetries    = 5
647:     baseBackoff   = 100 * time.Millisecond
648:     maxBackoff    = 30 * time.Second
649: )
650: 
651: // retryWithBackoff executes fn up to maxRetries times with exponential backoff.
652: // Returns the first nil error, or the last error if all retries are exhausted.
653: func retryWithBackoff(ctx context.Context, fn func() error) error {
654:     var lastErr error
655:     for attempt := 0; attempt <= maxRetries; attempt++ {
656:         if attempt > 0 {
657:             backoff := time.Duration(math.Pow(2, float64(attempt))) * baseBackoff
658:             if backoff > maxBackoff {
659:                 backoff = maxBackoff
660:             }
661:             log.Printf("retry: attempt %d/%d, backing off %v", attempt, maxRetries, backoff)
662:             select {
663:             case <-time.After(backoff):
664:             case <-ctx.Done():
665:                 return fmt.Errorf("retry cancelled: %w", ctx.Err())
666:             }
667:         }
668:         if err := fn(); err != nil {
669:             lastErr = err
670:             log.Printf("retry: attempt %d failed: %v", attempt, err)
671:             continue
672:         }
673:         return nil
674:     }
675:     return fmt.Errorf("all %d retries failed: %w", maxRetries, lastErr)
676: }
